title: 4.6 Methods of Birth Control
description: Natural and artificial methods of family planning including barrier, hormonal, surgical, and natural methods

questions.question: The deliberate prevention of pregnancy is called:
questions.explanation: Contraception is the deliberate prevention of pregnancy, which can be achieved in a number of ways.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most obvious natural method of preventing pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Abstinence involves a couple avoiding sexual intercourse and is the most obvious way of preventing pregnancy.

questions.question: The withdrawal method (coitus interruptus) involves:
options: Pulling the penis out before ejaculation
questions.correctAnswer: Pulling the penis out before ejaculation
questions.explanation: Withdrawal involves a man pulling his penis out of the vagina before ejaculation to prevent sperm from entering.

questions.question: What is the effectiveness of the withdrawal method with perfect use?
questions.explanation: Withdrawal effectiveness is 96% with perfect use and 82% with typical use.

questions.question: Fertility awareness methods rely on:
options: Understanding when ovulation is most likely
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding when ovulation is most likely
questions.explanation: Fertility awareness methods rely on understanding the most likely time that ovulation will take place during the monthly cycle.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of barrier method of contraception?
questions.explanation: Male condoms are a barrier method available in latex, lambskin, and polyurethane that prevent pregnancy by stopping sperm from entering the vagina.

questions.question: Male condoms made of lambskin are not recommended for infection prevention because:
options: They contain small pores that may permit passage of bacteria and viruses
questions.correctAnswer: They contain small pores that may permit passage of bacteria and viruses
questions.explanation: Lambskin condoms contain small pores that may permit the passage of bacteria and viruses, so they are not recommended for infection prevention.

questions.question: The effectiveness of male condoms with perfect use is:
questions.explanation: Male condom effectiveness is 98% with perfect use and 85% with typical use.

questions.question: A diaphragm is a thin rubber disc that is placed in the vagina to:
options: Cover the cervix and stop sperm entering the uterus
questions.correctAnswer: Cover the cervix and stop sperm entering the uterus
questions.explanation: A diaphragm covers the cervix and stops sperm from entering the uterus.

questions.question: Spermicides are chemicals that:
questions.explanation: Spermicides are chemicals that kill or immobilize sperm, though on their own they are not very reliable.

questions.question: The IUD (intra-uterine device) prevents pregnancy mainly by:
options: Preventing implantation of a fertilized ovum
questions.correctAnswer: Preventing implantation of a fertilized ovum
questions.explanation: The IUD is inserted into the wall of the uterus where it probably prevents implantation of a fertilized ovum.

questions.question: The effectiveness rate of the IUD is approximately:
questions.explanation: The IUD is about 98% effective.

questions.question: The contraceptive pill works by:
questions.explanation: The pill contains hormones that suppress ovulation and so prevent conception.

questions.question: The contraceptive pill needs to be taken for how many days between menstrual periods?
questions.explanation: The pills need to be taken each day for the 21 days between menstrual periods.

questions.question: The contraceptive implant is inserted under the skin of the upper arm and releases which hormone?
questions.explanation: The implant slowly releases the hormone progesterone, preventing pregnancy, and lasts for about 3 years.

questions.question: A contraceptive injection containing progesterone stays effective for between:
questions.explanation: The contraceptive injection contains progesterone and stays effective for between 8 and 12 weeks.

questions.question: Male sterilization is called:
questions.explanation: Vasectomy is a surgical operation in which the man's sperm ducts are cut and the ends sealed.

questions.question: After vasectomy, what happens to the sperm produced by the testes?
options: They are removed by white blood cells
questions.correctAnswer: They are removed by white blood cells
questions.explanation: The sperm are removed by white cells as fast as they form.

questions.question: Female sterilization involves tying, blocking, or cutting the:
questions.explanation: A woman may be sterilized by an operation in which her oviducts are tied, blocked, or cut — this is called tubal ligation or laparotomy.

questions.question: Both vasectomy and tubal ligation are considered:
options: Permanent, though sometimes reversible by microsurgery
Effective only for a few years
questions.correctAnswer: Permanent, though sometimes reversible by microsurgery
questions.explanation: Although tubal ligation and vasectomy are considered permanent, both procedures can in many cases be reversed by microsurgery.

questions.question: The IUS (intra-uterine system) differs from the IUD because it:
questions.explanation: The IUS is T-shaped and releases the hormone progesterone slowly over time, which prevents ovulation.

questions.question: Which hormone-based contraceptive method can provide protection for up to 5 years?
questions.explanation: The IUS releases progesterone slowly over a long period of time — up to 5 years.

questions.question: Monitoring body temperature helps in natural family planning because:
options: It predicts the exact day of menstruation
A woman's temperature rises by about 0.5 degrees Celsius during or soon after ovulation
questions.correctAnswer: A woman's temperature rises by about 0.5 degrees Celsius during or soon after ovulation
questions.explanation: During or soon after ovulation, a woman's temperature rises by about 0.5 degrees Celsius, helping identify the fertile period.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of natural family planning methods?
options: They require no cooperation from partners
questions.explanation: Natural methods have no side effects and are permitted by most religions.
